prospects.thesis: Leidos combines defense IT modernization with health and civil contracts, offering diversified exposure to sustained federal spending under the current defense budget environment. The stock's 1M momentum of +30.6% paired with a modest 1.0x P/S multiple suggests institutional re-rating is still in early innings, with bullish options flow confirming smart money positioning. Recent contract wins in AI-enabled defense analytics and cyber operations provide near-term earnings visibility.

AeroVironment is a pure-play on unmanned systems and loitering munitions — the fastest-growing sub-niche in defense given lessons from ongoing global conflicts and Pentagon Replicator program funding. The +35.6% 1M move reflects accelerating drone procurement orders, while bullish institutional positioning signals continued accumulation. Represents differentiated exposure from prime contractor LDOS, focused on tactical drone hardware.

Super Micro is the leading AI server integrator, benefiting directly from hyperscaler capex and liquid-cooled GPU rack demand tied to next-gen Blackwell deployments. The 0.7x P/S multiple is remarkably low for a company at the center of AI infrastructure buildout, suggesting the stock has recovered from prior accounting overhang without full multiple re-rating. Bullish options and institutional flow confirm the turnaround thesis is taking hold.

MongoDB's vector search capabilities position it as critical infrastructure for enterprise RAG and agentic AI workloads, driving accelerating Atlas cloud consumption. The +29.7% 1M move reflects renewed enterprise AI spending and shows institutional conviction returning after last year's growth deceleration concerns. Upcoming earnings could catalyze further re-rating if Atlas guidance improves.

UiPath is transitioning from traditional RPA to agentic automation, positioning it as an enterprise beneficiary of the shift from AI experimentation to production workflow deployment. At 4.7x P/S with a $7.8B cap, valuation is reasonable for a category leader with bullish options and institutional flow signaling renewed conviction. Differentiated from data-layer play MDB by targeting the process automation end of the AI stack.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: The clearest tell in this data is a classic defensive rotation dressed up as a rate-cut trade — big money is loading into Real Estate and Utilities with extreme call-heavy positioning, which almost always signals the smart money thinks the Fed is about to cut rates or that the economy is softening enough to force their hand. Energy calls are also getting bid, likely tied to the administration's continued push on domestic drilling permits and the ongoing Middle East risk premium, while Consumer Discretionary bullishness suggests some are betting the tariff drama gets negotiated down rather than escalated. On the other side, Financials are getting aggressively hedged with unusual put volume — that's a huge red flag because banks usually rally into rate cuts, so someone is worried about credit losses, regional bank exposure, or the fallout from stalled deregulation bills; Communication Services puts likely reflect antitrust anxiety around Google and Meta plus the ongoing Section 230 fights in Congress. The widening credit spreads and bearish HYG/LQD flow confirm the story: institutions are quietly preparing for a growth scare or credit event in the next 4-8 weeks, even as the headline indices grind higher. The contradiction worth noting is that bearish Consumer Staples positioning alongside bullish Utilities breaks the normal "defensive playbook" — that tells me this isn't a pure recession trade, it's specifically a *rates-down-but-consumer-still-spending* trade, possibly anticipating stimulus or tax legislation.
